thesis: Round 1 established that fresh 13F initiations are a weak signal even where the mapping works: 934 NEW disclosures across fourteen managers through as_of=2026-02-13, 22 tradeable, 912 lost to unmapped CUSIPs, and a 52% beat-benchmark rate among the ones that did map -- a coin flip whose mean was carried by two outliers. Round 2 asks whether that signal reaches this 93-symbol roster at all, and the honest answer is no. First, the empirical check the brief asked for: the CUSIP-to-ticker bridge is the user's own ledger (app.institutions.catalog.ledger_cusip_tickers), so I read every (cusip, primary_symbol) pair the ledger actually holds -- 119 rows, 119 unique tickers -- and intersected that set against the round-2 roster's 93 symbols. Six overlap: GDX, GDXJ, IGV, SLV, TLT, XBI. Not zero, which the brief said was a live empirical question rather than something to assume either way -- but not enough to build on, for a reason that shows up the moment you check what the fourteen managers actually hold. Querying load_latest(as_of=2026-02-13) for all fourteen catalog managers, only two hold any of those six tickers at all: BRIDGEWATER (IGV, weight 0.109% of a 1040-line book) and RENTECH (XBI 0.008%, GDX 0.006%, IGV 0.005% of a 3185-line book). The other twelve -- BRK, ARKINVEST, PERSHING, SCION, APPALOOSA, DUQUESNE, SOROS, THIRDPOINT, ELLIOTT, TIGERGLOBAL, COATUE, LONEPINE -- hold zero. Narrowing to what a momentum-on-fresh-initiations strategy actually needs, NEW rows specifically: across all 934 NEW disclosures in the most recent public delta for every manager (identical universe of filings to round 1's count, since as_of is unchanged), exactly 2 map to a round-2 roster ticker -- Bridgewater's IGV (new, 281,938 shares, 0.109% weight) and Rentech's XBI (new, 0.008% weight). Both are from the two books round 1's own thesis explicitly excluded as not comparable to a concentrated manager's conviction buy ("a NEW row there is a 0.01-0.5% sliver of an index-like or systematic book, not a decision") -- applying that same standard here rather than relaxing it because the sample got smaller, zero of the ten concentrated, genuinely stock-picking managers I would have trusted as a signal in round 1 have a single fresh initiation that reaches this roster. The ledger cannot name JNJ or XLU or TLT, as the brief predicted, and the two names it can name arrive at 0.005%-0.109% weight inside billion-line systematic macro books -- portfolio arithmetic, not a decision. Total holdings mapping loss across all fourteen managers' latest snapshots: 5071 holdings, 4 mapped to a round-2 roster ticker (0.08%), all four from the two excluded books. I looked for the mapping rather than assuming it away and found it is real but unusable -- this is the 'no, and here is what I did about it' the brief asked for. So this card carries no 13F signal at all; the discipline is still momentum, expressed as pure price-trend confirmation, standing on its own per the brief's explicit instruction. Mechanism: names the market has already started to trend tend to keep trending over multi-month horizons -- underreaction to slowly-diffusing information (analyst estimates and institutional flows adjust in stages, not on the print) and trend-following capital that arrives after a move is already underway, both documented cross-asset (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993 for single-name momentum, Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012 for time-series momentum across equities, bonds and commodities). The other side of the trade: value-discipline holders capping exposure into strength and short sellers fading a name that 'already ran,' both selling into a trend that has further to go before the market has fully re-rated it. I measured trailing-252-session return, 126-session (6-month) and 63-session (3-month) return, annualized volatility, and pct-of-days-above-sma(200) for all 93 round-2 symbols through 2026-02-13. Metals/thematic names (SLV +102% 126d, GDXJ +87%, GDX +80%, PPLT +51%) showed the strongest momentum by far but at 43-56% annualized volatility -- a single fixed stop_loss_pct cannot fit both that and a calmer name, per this brief's own engine-constraint warning, so I did not build on them; a metals-only card would be a legitimate but different strategy than the one asked for here. Instead I selected eight names in a comparable volatility band (19.1%-33.2% annualized, a 14-point spread versus the roster's full range of near-zero to 56%) that were simultaneously trending -- close above both sma(50) and sma(200) as of the cutoff, and 40%-99% of the trailing year spent above sma(200) -- and that measured genuinely diversified against each other: mean pairwise correlation 0.253 over the trailing 259 sessions (min 0.026, max 0.568), well under the 0.581 this brief measured for the round-2 sector-ETF cluster and the 0.589 round-1 measured for its semiconductor cluster. Universe, ordered by measured 126-session return (the tiebreak the brief flagged): CAT (industrials, +85.4%, 33.2% vol), JNJ (healthcare, +39.3%, 19.1% vol -- the exact name this brief said the ledger could not resolve, reached here on price alone, no 13F claim attached), XOM (energy, +38.3%, 24.8% vol), XBI (biotech, +37.2%, 27.9% vol), EWZ (Brazil equity, +36.5%, 25.0% vol), ICLN (clean energy, +34.9%, 24.4% vol), WMT (retail staple, +32.8%, 25.9% vol), NEE (utility, +29.8%, 26.6% vol) -- eight genuinely different sectors and one non-US-equity country fund, not eleven costumes on the same trade. Entry requires close > sma(50) and close > sma(200) and rsi(14) > 50: trend confirmed on two horizons plus a momentum floor, deliberately unoptimized and structurally identical to the trend filter round 1 validated conceptually (there, filtering a 13F-curated list; here, filtering the whole selection). Exit is a trend break (close crosses_below sma(50)), backed by a 10% stop and a 120-day time stop so the position cannot ride a slow bleed indefinitely if the trend-break rule is late to fire. What I did differently from round 1, and why: round 1 used 13F to pick a universe and price rules to time entry. Round 2 could not do that -- the mapping check above shows the 13F leg contributes nothing on this roster -- so the universe selection itself is now driven by the same measured momentum/trend/diversification criteria that round 1 only applied inside the entry rule. This is not a refusal to use the new freedom the round-2 roster offers; it is a direct consequence of checking the constraint the brief asked me to check, finding it binding, and building the strategy the discipline can actually support instead of forcing a thin 13F narrative onto two 0.01%-weight portfolio-management rows in billion-line macro books. What I expect to go wrong: momentum strategies crash together in a correlated risk-off shock -- CAT, XOM, EWZ and ICLN all carry real cyclical/growth-factor exposure that measured low pairwise correlation in a trending 2024-2026 regime but has historically converged toward 1 in a broad selloff (2022, 2020-Q1), which the 259-session correlation window used here cannot see because it barely includes such an episode. XBI and ICLN are the most volatile names in the set and have the fastest, sharpest mean-reversion crashes in this roster's history when a multi-month run ends -- a stop evaluated on the previous close, not the intraday low, will be late and expensive exactly when that happens. EWZ carries country-specific political and currency risk with no relationship to US price trend at all. And the entry rule is the same simple trend-and-momentum filter this discipline always uses: it will underperform, possibly badly, in a choppy, range-bound regime with no sustained trend in any of these eight names, which six months is not enough time to rule out.
entry: close > sma(50) and close > sma(200) and rsi(14) > 50
